title: CDK Global Taps Indian-Origin Veteran Sudhakar Ramakrishna as CEO
excerpt: Ramakrishna, former SolarWinds chief executive, succeeds Brian MacDonald at the Brookfield-owned automotive retail software company, taking charge on October 5 as CDK pushes its AI-driven dealership platform.
body:
• CDK Global has named Sudhakar Ramakrishna president and CEO, effective October 5, 2026, with a seat on the company's board of directors. He succeeds Brian MacDonald, who is retiring and will serve as senior strategic advisor to Brookfield and CDK.
  • Ramakrishna previously served as president and CEO of SolarWinds from January 2021 and led Pulse Secure before that; his three-decade career includes senior roles at Citrix, Polycom, Motorola and 3Com, an MS in computer science from Kansas State and a management degree from Northwestern's Kellogg School.
  • CDK, owned by Brookfield's private equity group, says it has invested more than $500 million over several years to turn its automotive retail platform from a "system of record" into a "system of intelligence and engagement," backed by 257 million unique customer IDs.

CDK Global, the automotive retail software provider owned by Brookfield's private equity arm, has put an Indian-origin technology veteran in charge. Sudhakar Ramakrishna took over as president and chief executive officer on October 5, succeeding Brian MacDonald, who retired after leading a multi-year turnaround of the company, CDK announced from Austin, Texas.

Ramakrishna also joins CDK's board of directors. MacDonald will stay on as a senior strategic advisor to Brookfield and CDK, providing continuity and perspective through the planned transition.

"Sudhakar is the right leader to build on that foundation. His experience leading technology organizations, scaling innovation and commercializing customer-centric products makes him well suited to advance CDK's momentum."

— Doug Bayerd, Managing Partner, Brookfield Private Equity Group

Context & Background

The appointment was announced on August 27, with the October 5 start date set for a clean handover. MacDonald had returned to CDK at what Brookfield called "an important moment" and led a multi-year transformation that the private equity owner says strengthened the company's strategy, product roadmap and financial foundation.

https://x.com/businessline/status/2107459693366931846

Ramakrishna arrives with nearly 30 years in enterprise software. He joined SolarWinds as president and CEO in January 2021, leading the infrastructure management software provider after running Pulse Secure, where he worked with customers and partners in complex, mission-critical environments. Earlier stops include senior vice president and general manager of Citrix's enterprise and service provider division, and leadership posts at Polycom, Motorola, 3Com and U.S. Robotics. He earned a master's in computer science from Kansas State University in 1991 and a master's in management from Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management in 1999.

Impact & Analysis

CDK sits at the center of American car retail: its software runs dealership management systems, digital retailing and customer-relationship tools across thousands of dealership rooftops. The company says it has invested more than $500 million over several years to evolve its platform from an industry "system of record" into what it calls a system of intelligence and engagement — embedding AI, analytics and customer insights directly into dealer workflows.

Its raw material is data. CDK says its platform holds 257 million unique customer IDs, reflecting most U.S. consumers and vehicles. As car buying shifts online and dealers lean on automation for pricing, inventory and service, that data becomes the foundation for AI products — the exact territory Ramakrishna has worked in across cloud, security and networking.

The leadership change also underscores Brookfield's long game. Since taking CDK private, the firm has bet that dealership software can be rebuilt around AI rather than disrupted by it. Hiring a CEO who has run both a public software company and a private-equity-backed cybersecurity firm fits that thesis.

"I look forward to spending time with our customers, learning from our teams and partners, and carrying forward our commitment to earning the industry's trust every day."

— Sudhakar Ramakrishna, President and CEO, CDK Global

Diaspora Angle

Ramakrishna joins a growing roster of Indian-origin executives running major U.S. technology companies. His path — a computer science master's at Kansas State in the early 1990s, a Kellogg MBA, then a steady climb through 3Com, Motorola, Citrix and Pulse Secure to the CEO's office at SolarWinds — tracks the generation of Indian engineers who came to the U.S. for graduate school in the 1990s and rose through enterprise software's ranks.

What's Next

Watch the product roadmap. CDK has framed its next phase around AI-driven engagement for dealers, and Ramakrishna's first moves — customer visits, leadership hires, and any acceleration of the platform's AI rollout — will signal how fast Brookfield wants that transformation to go. MacDonald's advisory role should keep the transition smooth, but the dealership industry's shift toward digital-first retail leaves little room for a slow start.
